Public Portion 
 1. Continued Discussions on the Woodland Ordinance 
On October 27, 2026, the Sustainability and Environment Committee, chaired by Councilor 
Victor Davila, met to continue reviewing the proposed Urban Woodlands Ordinance. 
Representatives of SCANS presented recommended revisions to the Law Department's draft, 
including technical corrections, procedures allowing applicants to amend applications during 
commission review, simplified tree assessment methods for larger properties, and limitations on 
fee waivers. Additional recommendations addressed incorporating climate change mitigation into 
the ordinance's definitions and review criteria, protecting existing trees and root systems during 
development, and ensuring that application fees and penalties appropriately reflect administrative 
costs and compliance requirements. 
 
The Law Department reviewed the recommendations and discussed potential revisions to 
application procedures, fee structures, waiver provisions, and climate mitigation standards. City 
Forester Alex Sherman raised concerns regarding the Forestry Division's capacity to administer 
and enforce the ordinance with existing staffing levels. He identified the potential need for 
additional field and administrative personnel. Discussion included the proposed Urban 
Woodlands Commission's structure, available grant funding, and opportunities to support 
implementation without placing an excessive financial burden on the City. Councilor Zaida 
Govan requested a preliminary budget outlining the resources needed to establish and administer 
the commission, and Sherman agreed to prepare an estimate. 
 
The Law Department was asked to review the proposed amendments and incorporate applicable 
revisions into the draft ordinance. Councilor Davila indicated his intention to advance the 
ordinance for initial City Council consideration before the end of the year while continuing to 
address implementation concerns. The committee scheduled a follow-up meeting for November 
9, 2026, at 4:00 p.m., to review the revised draft and staffing considerations. No formal vote or 
recommendation to the full City Council was recorded. The meeting concluded at 4:55 p.m.
